an1.11:1.1: “Feature of beauty” is _subhanimitta_. In early Pali, _nimitta_ is used for a feature or quality of the mind that, when focused on, promotes the growth of similar or related qualities. Thus focusing on beauty fosters the desire for that beauty. | In this chapter, the five hindrances are divided into one per Sutta to produce five Suttas, then the positive side is given, with another five Suttas. Compare [sn46.2]() and [an3.68](). | The “single thing” template recurs throughout this chapter, and is alos found occasionally in the Saṁyutta ([sn45.77:1.2](), [sn46.29:1.1]()).
an1.11:1.2: To “apply the mind irrationally” is to use the mind so as to produce the opposite effect than that desired.
